subject: Post-demo: latency vs. cost checklist and buyer map
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@mediscalehealth.com>, Tom Huang <tom.huang@mediscalehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: latency vs. cost checklist and buyer map

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for your time today. Great discussion and appreciate the transparency on constraints. I wanted to capture the follow-ups and a short checklist so we can map next internal steps on your side. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Summary from the demo (2 key asks):
- Primary objective: integrate model-based clinical note summarization and triage rules into existing intake flow. Production traffic target: ~2000 requests/day initial, expected to grow 3x in 6 months.
- Main constraints: must keep PII/PHI in-house where required, latency for the triage call needs to be tight (user-facing), and procurement will need fixed pricing or predictable committed spend for Dedicated/Private options.

Clarification requests / decision criteria we need to lock down:
1) Latency SLO: do you want 95th-percentile under 250ms (preferred) or is 95th under 500ms acceptable if cost is materially lower? Please indicate the target and whether 99th is relevant.
2) Deployment mode preference: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private (VPC/on-prem). You mentioned data residency; can you confirm whether Private is mandatory for PHI workflows or if VPC Private would suffice?
3) Security/compliance gates: which docs are must-haves for procurement? SOC 2 Type II, KMS integration, and audit logs were mentioned — anything else (e.g., penetration test report, BAAs)?
4) Procurement timeline & economic buyer: who signs contracts (name + role/email), and what is your target procurement window?
5) Cost guardrails: do you have a per-month committed budget range or target unit economics (e.g., $ / 1M tokens or $ / request) we should model?

Attached: redwood-demo-deck.pdf (deck), pq-latency-benchmark.csv (sample latency numbers from similar workloads), SOW-template.docx (starter).

Next steps I propose:
- Samira: confirm the answers to 1–4 above and share procurement contact.
- Karthik: I’ll follow up with a Dedicated vs Private cost sketch for the expected QPS and token counts.
- Jordan: I’ll loop you on SOC 2 / security artifacts once we have the procurement contact.

If easier, we can schedule a 30-min carve-out next week to go through the checklist with procurement + security. Are you available next Tue/Wed morning PST?

Thanks —

Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene.ch@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

Cc: Tom Huang <tom.huang@mediscalehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@mediscalehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency vs. cost checklist and buyer map

Irene —

Thanks for the write-up, that’s super helpful. Quick answers below (feel free to forward to procurement/security folks):

1) Latency SLO: Our product team needs a hard cap for interactive triage flows. Target: 95th <= 300ms. 99th should be < 750ms but it is less critical for now. If we can get a clear cost delta between 300ms vs 500ms targets that would help.

2) Deployment mode: For initial pilot (non-PHI subset) Hosted is fine. For any workflows touching PHI, we need Private (VPC) or on-prem. So our preferred path: Hosted for pilot -> Dedicated/Private for full rollout.

3) Security/compliance: Must-haves for procurement: SOC 2 Type II report, BAA (we will need a BAA for PHI), KMS/HSM key control options, audit logs retention 1 year, and your latest pen test summary.

4) Economic buyer & procurement timeline:
- Economic buyer: Tom Huang, VP of Product <tom.huang@mediscalehealth.com> (he has final sign-off).
- Procurement contact: procurement@mediscalehealth.com (they handle SOWs and PO).
- Timeline: Targeting procurement kickoff in ~3 weeks; pilot agreement before end of June.

5) Cost guardrails: We don’t have a firm committed budget yet. For procurement conversations, assume a conservative annual committed range: $80k–$200k depending on deployment mode. Please model both a pilot (monthly $6k–$12k) and a committed Dedicated scenario.

Next step for you: a short cost sketch (hosted vs dedicated vs private) based on our current traffic estimate and a one-page security artifact list (SOC2, BAA process, KMS options). I’ll loop procurement and Tom on the follow-up.

Thanks —

Samira Patel
Head of Product Integrations | MediScale Health
samira.patel@mediscalehealth.com
